root_cause.text: The RISC-V IOMMU paging-domain code updated DDT/PDT entries in `riscv_iommu_iodir_update()` without issuing the mandatory IOTINVAL invalidations, so stale TLB/context-cache entries could remain valid after descriptor changes.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a new helper `riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval()` specifically “to perform required TLB and context cache invalidations after modifying DDT or PDT entries” and calls it immediately after `riscv_iommu_cmd_iodir_inval_ddt()` in `riscv_iommu_iodir_update()`, which shows the original code was missing these required invalidations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add specification-compliant IOTINVAL handling for IODIR updates to invalidate stale IOMMU entries after DDT/PDT modifications.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function, riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval(), was added. It initializes an IOTINVAL command, inspects iohgatp mode and the DDT/PDT-related fields in dc and pc, conditionally sets PSCID and GSCID fields in the command for several cases, and then sends the command. A comment was also added describing the function's purpose and referencing the RISC-V IOMMU specification.
intent_record.how: The new function issues the appropriate IOTINVAL invalidation command after DDT or PDT entry changes, with different parameter combinations depending on whether the IOMMU is in bare mode or translated mode and whether PDT invalidation is requested. This ensures stale IOMMU translations are invalidated according to the specification, preventing devices from using outdated mappings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an IOTINVAL during IODIR updates to invalidate stale translation state for the current domain configuration.
intent_record.what: A new call to `riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval(iommu, false, dc->iohgatp, dc, NULL);` was inserted immediately after sending the IODIR invalidate-DDT command and setting the DID, along with an explanatory comment about SVA/PASID not yet being merged and the default `inval_pdt=false` and `pc=NULL` configuration.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this makes the IOMMU perform an additional IOTINVAL operation for the domain/device context during IODIR updates, ensuring any stale I/O translation state is invalidated using the current `iohgatp` and a null process context. This extends the existing update flow to cover translation invalidation that was previously omitted.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an IOTINVAL step to the IODIR update path for the current default SVA/PASID-less configuration.
intent_record.what: A new call to `riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval(iommu, false, dc->iohgatp, dc, NULL);` was added inside the loop after sending the IODIR invalidate command and before the final command sync, along with an explanatory comment about SVA/PASID not yet being merged and the default `inval_pdt=false` and `pc=NULL` configuration.
intent_record.how: At runtime, each IODIR update now also triggers an IOTINVAL operation with a fixed non-invalidate-PDT setting and a null PASID context, ensuring the IOMMU invalidation sequence is issued for the current domain/device state. This changes behavior by actively invalidating translation state in the current default configuration rather than only updating the directory entry.

grouping_result.intent: Add an IOTINVAL step to the IODIR update path for the current default SVA/PASID-less configuration.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add IOTINVAL handling to the IODIR update path to invalidate stale IOMMU translation state after directory updates in the current default configuration.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the described root cause by adding the missing IOTINVAL invalidations in the IODIR update path after DDT/PDT changes, preventing stale TLB/context-cache entries from persisting.

candidates.rationale: This statement programs the IODIR/DDT entry for the device, which changes directory translation state. In the vulnerable code path it was performed without the required IOTINVAL invalidation, leaving stale TLB/context-cache entries valid after the update.
This sends the DDT/PDT update command without any accompanying invalidation step. The root cause is that the update path executed this command alone, so stale translation state could persist.
This is the directory update operation in the default configuration path. Before the fix it occurred without the mandatory IOTINVAL, which is the direct cause of stale IOMMU translation entries.
The command was issued to update the IODIR entry but no invalidation followed before or after it in the vulnerable version. This omission allowed outdated cached translations to remain usable.

vuln_statements.explanation: This command applies the IODIR/DDT/PDT update, but in the vulnerable code path it was executed without the mandatory IOTINVAL invalidation. That omission is the root cause of stale TLB/context-cache entries remaining valid after descriptor changes.

This statement programs the directory translation entry that changes device translation state. In the vulnerable version it was part of the update path that lacked the required IOTINVAL, allowing stale translation state to persist.

commit 488ffbf181718b9ad8c1838cb249d60973e78eda
Author: Tomasz Jeznach <tomasz.jeznach@linux.dev>
Date:   Tue Oct 15 23:52:19 2024 -0700

    iommu/riscv: Paging domain support
    
    Introduce first-stage address translation support.
    
    Page table configured by the IOMMU driver will use the highest mode
    implemented by the hardware, unless not known at the domain allocation
    time falling back to the CPU’s MMU page mode.
    
    This change introduces IOTINVAL.VMA command, require
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body already contains explicit invalidation handling for device-directory updates, which is the fix for the root cause. In `riscv_iommu_iodir_update()` the code no longer just updates `dc->tc`; it first clears validity and sends an invalidation: `WRITE_ONCE(dc->tc, tc & ~RISCV_IOMMU_DC_TC_V);`, then `riscv_iommu_cmd_iodir_inval_ddt(&cmd);`, `riscv_iommu_cmd_iodir_set_did(&cmd, fwspec->ids[i]);`, and `riscv_iommu_cmd_send(iommu, &cmd);`. After the loop it also performs `riscv_iommu_cmd_sync(iommu, RISCV_IOMMU_IOTINVAL_TIMEOUT);`. This means the mandatory invalidation is present, so the vulnerable construct (updating DDT/PDT entries without IOTINVAL) is not present in this commit version.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet already contains explicit invalidation logic around device-context updates, so the vulnerable construct (updating DDT/PDT entries without IOTINVAL) is not present here. In `riscv_iommu_iodir_update()` the code does not just write the new context; it first invalidates old cached device-context values: `riscv_iommu_cmd_iodir_inval_ddt(&cmd); ... riscv_iommu_cmd_send(iommu, &cmd);` and then, after programming the new context, it again issues invalidation and a sync: `/* Invalidate device context after update */ ... riscv_iommu_cmd_send(iommu, &cmd); ... riscv_iommu_cmd_sync(iommu, RISCV_IOMMU_IOTINVAL_TIMEOUT);`. The commit message also states: `This change introduces IOTINVAL.VMA command, required to invalidate any cached IOATC entries after mapping is updated and/or removed from the paging domain.` That shows the mandatory invalidation handling is already implemented in this version, so this function does contain the fix and not the vulnerable omission.
